full_judgment:
11. It is stated that bidhi 17 of the Bidhimala provides that an employee will not get pension benefits at the time of retirement if he is removed or suspended from the service or there is any departmental proceeding or criminal case pending against the employee or he is found guilty of misconduct in any departmental proceeding or for any other offence . It is further stated that neither during his long service in the Biman nor at the time of his retirement there was any departmental proceeding or any criminal case pending against the petitioner. 

 12. It is stated that by Memo No. DAKGF /P-31198/2011/853 dated 24-4-2011 issued under the signature of the Assistant Manager personally, the petitioner was sanctioned 6(six) months LPR as per the provisions of bidhi 14 of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Karmachari (Obasor Vhata and Anutoshik) Bidhimala 1988 and his retirement would be effective on 14-9-2011 with the said memo a clearance certificate form was attached and the petitioner was requested to obtain clearance from all the concerned departments for final settlement of his accounts. It is further stated that the above act of the respondents clearly proves that there was neither any departmental proceeding nor any criminal case pending against the petitioner at the time of his retirement. 

 22. Mr, AZM Mohiuddin the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that as per provision of bidhi 17 of the Bidhimala provides that an employee will not get pension benefits at the time of retirement if he is removed or suspended from the service or there is any departmental proceeding or any case pending against the employee or he is found guilty of misconduct in any departmental proceeding or for any other offence. Since no such departmental proceeding or any case was pending against the petitioner at the time of his retirement the respondents are liable to be directed to pay the gratuity, provident fund and pension benefits of the petitioner as per law. 

 23. He further submitted that the service of the petitioner is guided by the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulations, 1979 and Bangladesh Biman Corporation Karmachari (Obosor Vhata and Anutoshik) Bidhimala, 1988 but no where within the 4 (four) corners of the said Regulations and Bidhimala it has empowered the authority to withhold his retirement benefits and other service benefits in the absence of any pending departmental proceeding or any case against him and, as such, the respondents are liable to be directed to pay the gratuity, provident fund and pension benefits of the petitioner as per law. 

 28. On the other hand the learned Deputy Attorney-General Khondaker Diliruzzaman appearing for the respondent No. 2 submits that in the paragraph No. 15 of the writ petition is not correct hence denied. With regard to the same it is stated that as per the practice of Biman retired employee is given a Clearance Form to take clearance from certain departments which does not include Finance Department. After obtaining clearance for the said Departments/sections the matter was forwarded to Pay Rolls section to prepare a final settlement of Accounts. Then the matter will be forwarded to Audit Section and after the Audit Clearance the matter will be forwarded to finance department for clearance and payment of the same. He further submits that in the case of the petitioner when the Pay Roll section prepared his final settlement of accounts and the Audit Department while certificates the same informed the management that Audit was not done for the period of September 2009 to April 2010 as such decision of the Finance Department will be final regarding the financial activities of the aforesaid period. He next submits that during the tenure of the petitioner as the Finance Manager, Karachi the Petitioner recovered Federal Excise Duty from the petitioner of Karachi to Dhaka Sector but he supplied the Income Tax Authority of Pakistan the passenger list of Karachi to Dhaka and Dhaka to Karachi Sectors. As a result the Income Tax Authority of Pakistan claimed Pakistani Rupees 631,96,632 as FED together with Pakistani Rupees 2,18,21,095 as Interest and 50,000 as fine. Biman filed application before the Appellate Tribunal of Income Tax Pakistan for exoneration of the aforesaid amount. But the said Tribunal rejected Biman's application. Thereafter Biman filed court case before the Hon'ble Sindh High Court of Pakistan regarding the aforesaid matter vide case No. SP.FEDR/ A-04/2012. The aforesaid case is still pending for adjudication. If Biman defeated in the aforesaid case, the petitioner has to bear the liability caused due to his professional omission and negligence as well. As a result of the aforesaid facts Biman finance Department did not give their clearance on the final settlement of the petitioner pending adjudication of the aforesaid case by the Hon'ble Sindh High Court of Pakistan 4. This fact has already been informed to the petitioner vide letter dated 25-7-2012 and the rule is liable to be discharged. 

 29. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates both the sides and perused the writ petition, the annexures 8, 9 and 10 so have been annexed with the writ petition and the affidavit-in-opposition thereto. Bangladesh Biman Carporation Employees (Service) Regulation, 1979 and the Bidhimala made under the said regulation goes to show that an employee after completion of his service at the time of retirement will get gratuity, provident fund and pension benefits. Rule 17 of the Bidhimala provides that no retirement benefit will be given to an employee of the Corporation if he was suspended or removed from the service or there is any departmental proceeding or criminal case pending against him or he has been found guilty of misconduct or any other offence. Mererso, the respondent No. 2 failed to point out that there is any departmental proceeding pending against the petitioner. As such, said provision is not applicable in the case of the petitioner. 

 30. The Rule is contested by respondent No. 2 duly authorized by the Managing Director and CEO of Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited by Government. The affidavit-in-opposition contending inter alia that as per the practice of Biman retired employee is given a Clearance Form to take clearance from certain departments which does not include Finance Department. After obtaining clearance for the said Departments/sections the matter was forwarded to Pay Rolls section to prepare a final settlement of Accounts. Then the matter will be forwarded to Audit Section and after the Audit Clearance the matter will be forwarded to finance department for clearance and payment of the same. It is further stated that in the case of the petitioner when the Pay Roll section prepared his final settlement of accounts and the Audit Department while certifies the same informed the management that Audit was not done for the period of September 2009 to April 2010 as such decision of the Finance Department will be final regarding the financial activities of the aforesaid period. It is further stated that during the tenure of the petitioner as the Finance Manager, Karachi the Petitioner recovered Federal Excise Duty from the petitioner of Karachi to Dhaka Sector but he supplied the Income Tax Authority of Pakistan the passenger list of Karachi to Dhaka and Dhaka to Karachi Sectors. As a result the Income Tax Authority of Pakistan claimed Pakistani Rupees 631,96,631 as FED together with Pakistani Rupees 2,18,21,095 as Interest and 50,000 as fine. Biman filed application before the Appellate Tribunal of Income Tax Pakistan for exoneration of the aforesaid amount. But the said Tribunal rejected Biman's application. Thereafter Biman filed court case before the Hon'ble Sindh High Court of Pakistan regarding the aforesaid matter vide Case No. SP FED R/A-04/2012. The aforesaid case is still pending for adjudication. If Biman defeated in the aforesaid case, the petitioner has to bear the liability caused due to his professional omission and negligence as well. As a result of the aforesaid facts Biman Finance Department did not give their clearance on the final settlement of the petitioner pending adjudication of the aforesaid case by the Hon'ble Sindh High Court of Pakistan 4. This fact has already been informed to the petitioner vide letter dated 25-7-2012. 

 31. It is apparent on the face of the record that the Corporation without any lawful reason just to fulfill their ulterior motive and to harass the petitioner withheld his service benefits which is legally entitled to on attaining the age of superannuation. The statement made in paragraph No. 10 of the affidavit-in-opposition, concerning the statements made in paragraph 22 to 28 of the writ petition, are totally misleading, misconceived and misrepresentation of facts and therefore, denied. The alleged claim of Rs. 8,50,67,727 are related to charging federal Excise duly (FED) by Pakistan Tax Authority upon the Incoming Passengers at Karachi Airport and the similar problems were also being faced by the other Air Line Operation in Pakistan. But the respondent No. 2 is trying to impose the said disputed claim upon the petitioner after his retirement from service on 14-11-2011, which is arbitrary and malafide. We find the service benefit of the petitioner cannot be withheld simply on the ground of the pendency of the application. Bangladesh Biman Airlines without any lawful reasons withheld the service benefits of the petitioner at the time of retirement simply on the plea on the pendency of an application before the appellate tribunal of an contact for exhortations Rs. 8,509,67,227. We find the service benefit of the petitioner cannot be withheld simply on the ground of the pendency of the application of Bangladesh Biman Airlines before the Honourable High Court of Pakistan without any reasons and the respondents are liable to pay the gratuity, pension and provident fund service benefits of the petitioner as per law. The very contact and Act of the respondent to withheld the service benefits of the petitioner is in violation of the Article 31 of the Constitution People's Republic of Bangladesh. So, Article 31 of the Constitution Republic of Bangladesh this Court in exercising its jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution is competent enough to enforce the fundamental right of the petitioner which is intended to be infringed by the respondents. 

 32. Having regard to the above facts we are of the view that the Corporation without any lawful reason withheld the service benefits of the petitioner at the time of the retirement. The Bangladesh Biman Airlines cannot withheld the service benefits of the petitioner for a indefinite period only on the ground of the pendency of the application before the Honour'ble High Court of Pakistan. Since there was no departmental proceeding or criminal case pending at the time of retirement of the petitioner, in view of the provisions of the Regulation and the Bidhimala the petitioner is entitled to get his gratuity, provident fund and pension benefits in accordance with law.
